                payload: Record<string, unknown> | null;
                question: string | null;
                recipient: string | null;
                result: unknown;
                status: "running" | "asking" | "failed" | "finished";
                thread_id: string | null;

                caller_interaction_ids: string[];

                expiry_at: string | null;
                interaction_id: string;
                interaction_ids: string[];
                resume_owner: string | null;
            };
        };
    }>;

    readonly baseUrl: string;
    readonly constants: {

        readonly PERSON_KIND: "person";

};

                readonly properties: {
                    readonly content: {
                        readonly anyOf: readonly [{

    readonly CallbackSchema: {

    readonly ChannelTemplate: {

A template with no runtime arguments carries no ``parameters``; a present\n``parameters`` is a non-empty dict.";

            readonly OverlapPolicy: {
                readonly description: "How a route treats a running turn and the newer participant messages that overlap it.\n\nGoverns participant MESSAGE turns on one thread only (``origin=\"client\"``,\n``inbound_kind=\"message\"``); an event turn always runs as its own turn. Two knobs and a\nwindow:\n\n* ``running`` — what happens to the turn in flight when a newer message is accepted:\n  ``continue`` leaves it running (one turn per message), ``cancel`` cancels it cooperatively\n  in favour of the newer message.\n* ``deliver`` — what a turn carries: ``one`` exactly one message per turn, ``all`` every\n  message accepted since the last turn started, in order, as one turn.\n* ``settle_seconds`` — a turn starts no earlier than this many seconds after its lead\n  message was accepted, so a burst inside the window rides in one turn. ``0`` disables it.\n\nThe default policy (``continue``/``one``/``0``) runs one turn per message and leaves the\npayload unchanged. Frozen.";
                readonly properties: {
                    readonly deliver: {
                        readonly default: "one";
                        readonly enum: readonly ["one", "all"];
                        readonly title: "Deliver";
                        readonly type: "string";
                    };
                    readonly running: {
                        readonly default: "continue";

                        readonly title: "Running";
                        readonly type: "string";
                    };
                    readonly settle_seconds: {
                        readonly default: 0;
                        readonly description: "Seconds a turn waits after its lead message was accepted before it starts, so a burst inside the window rides one turn; 0 disables the window.";
                        readonly maximum: 30;
                        readonly minimum: 0;
                        readonly title: "Settle Seconds";
                        readonly type: "integer";

                readonly type: "object";

        readonly description: "The persisted body of a versioned preset.\n\n``base_tool`` is the tool the preset binds; ``description`` is the preset's\nhuman description; ``fixed_kwargs`` are the baked kwargs (each becomes a\nhidden, fixed constant on the bound tool). ``extensions`` is a list of\nextension COMBOS — the SAME shape as a manifest ``extensions`` map value,\neach combo element an extension name or a ``{\"name\", \"config\"}`` mapping\nbinding author config (e.g. an ``ask_external`` verifier) — fed unconverted\nto the structured runtime-attach API at register (an empty outer list means\nno extensions; an empty INNER combo is rejected by the validating view).\n``output_schema`` is an optional author-set OUTPUT JSON Schema (an object\nschema): on an AGENT base it is baked into the run tool's ``response_format``\nso the agent FORCES a structured output matching it; on a plain tool it is\nadvertised as the bound tool's output schema and every result is validated\nagainst it at run time — a park is a suspend signal, not a result, and passes.\n``input_schema`` is an optional author-set INPUT JSON\nSchema: it becomes the exposed named tool's input contract, and the caller's\nvalidated object is routed into the base tool's declared payload argument (see\n:class:`PresetInputSchemaSupport`). Only a base tool that DECLARES input-schema\nsupport accepts one; otherwise a set ``input_schema`` is a loud authoring error.\n\nEach schema is the ``TemplatedText | dict`` union: an inline ``dict`` is the JSON\nSchema document itself; a :class:`~tai42_contract.template.TemplatedText` names a stored\nschema by ``id`` (or carries it inline as ``content``), rendered and parsed as JSON to the\nsame schema at the point of use and save.\n\nEvery field must survive carry-forward on a version save: dropping\n``extensions`` would make the branch tools vanish on reload, dropping\n``base_tool`` would break the bind, dropping ``description`` would strip the\ntool's description, dropping ``output_schema`` would silently un-enforce the\nstructured output, and dropping ``input_schema`` would silently un-enforce the\nstructured input.\n\nA ``fixed_kwargs`` scalar-string value written ``!ENV ${VAR}`` is a SECRET\nREFERENCE, not a credential: the server resolves it from the environment at bind\nand the store keeps only the reference — never the resolved value.";
